## Steps

A story can have steps: one or more further prompts, each a piece of the story done after the one before, as a chain's steps are. Each step has a prompt, a mode of its own, Code or Spec, starting as the story's, and a model and effort, starting as the story's, and may have attachments. A story with no steps is just its own prompt, as before; its prompt is always its first step.
A story's steps are always listed whole, every step in one list, never its prompt apart and the rest beneath it: its own prompt is step 1, a row of the list like the others, and each further step follows it, numbered from 2. An open story lists all its steps this way, in order, each row with its number, its mode pill, and the first line of its prompt, opening in place to edit, as a story does. "Add step", beneath the last, adds one at the end, open and focused; several can be added one after another, Enter in an empty step's prompt adding none. Steps are reordered by dragging, as the [DragReorderBehaviour](../../ui/behaviours/drag-reorder/index.md#drag-reorder-behaviour) says, or Alt+Up and Alt+Down, and each has a remove button in its row and in its menu. The story's own prompt stays first and can't be moved among them.
A step belongs to its story and to nothing else. It is saved in the story's file, in a `steps` list of the story's hidden anchor, in its order, and saved as every change to the plan is, straight away; a story duplicated copies its steps, and one deleted deletes them. Its order is kept wherever the story goes, between sections, into a sprint, and back from Done.
Wherever the story is shown, its steps are too: its card in Planning shows how many beneath its title, muted, counting every step, its prompt among them, so a prompt with two further steps reads "3 steps", with the whole list in its tooltip, step 1 first; the open story lists them as above; a proposal to add to it shows them, so what it would add to can be seen; and once it is sent, it is sent as a chain, its prompt first and each step after it in order, each step sent only once the one before it finishes, as the [PromptEditor](../prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor)'s chained tasks are, so the Tasks tab shows the story as one chain with its steps beneath it. A story sent can't be given more steps; its steps, sent or still to come, read as they were sent. In Current sprint, a story with steps lists its steps on its card, beneath its title, a line for each step, step 1, its own prompt, first, then every other in order, each with its number, the first line of its prompt cut off with an ellipsis, and its own status, as a running chain's are in the Tasks tab; in Done, and in a finding started from the story, its steps are listed the same way, collapsed to its step count until it is expanded. The same steps, in the same order, are what every place shows, since every place reads them from the story's own file.
A step is only ever added to a story that exists. Adding one to a story that doesn't, as one deleted while a proposal naming it waited, or by another window, or whose file was removed from `.suspense/planning/` meanwhile, changes nothing: no story is made for it, no other story is given it, and nothing is saved. It says so in plain words where it was asked for, as "That story no longer exists, so the step wasn't added", in the theme's error colour, as the states say, with what was to be added kept, so it can be added to another story or as a new one. A step added to a story already sent is refused the same way, saying the story has been sent.

## Drafting

Drafting stories shows its work in one place, the side panel, docked at the board's right, as the layout places it, replacing whatever it held, never in a popup that hides the list. It has the request box at its top, labelled "Describe what you want", and beneath it, while the run goes, its research: a muted line of what the harness is doing, as "Reading the spec…", with its spinner, updating as it goes, and a "Stop" button. Once it ends, the panel lists its proposals, as below, then "Accept all" and "Reject all" buttons along the panel's foot, and closes itself once none is left to decide. A run that fails shows its error, as the states say, and leaves the request in its box to try again; one that proposes nothing says so, as an empty state. Proposals are kept until each is decided, so closing Planning and coming back finds them as they were.
Drafting can also be started from an open story, with "Ask agent" in its card's menu or the open story's footer: the request box then reads "What does this story need?", the run is told the story's title and prompt, and the drafting panel takes the open story's place in the side panel, the story's card staying highlighted while the draft is about it.
A draft about a story, from "Ask agent" or "Draft with agent", may propose rewriting it: a proposal whose target is the story itself, to be rewritten, its title, prompt, mode, and spec citations replaced by the proposal's, its steps and attachments kept; as well as additions to it, each a step, as the proposals say. Where a story holds more than one piece of work, the draft splits it: the story's rewrite comes first, the first piece, with its steps, and each other piece is a proposal for a new story of its own, its target "New story", with its own title, prompt, mode, and spec citations, grounded as the spec grounding says. A story that is one piece of work gets only its rewrite and its steps, and no new story.
A draft favours several stories over one story of many steps. Each story it proposes is one piece of work a single chain does: as a rule a Chain story, its prompt changing the spec and then the code to match it, with at most one step, a Spec step following the chain up, where the spec needs settling once the code is done. Work that would need more than that is split into stories of their own, each a "New story" proposal, never strung onto one story as further steps. Another mode, Code, Spec, Ask, or Freeform, is proposed only for a story that is only that, as a question or a change to the code alone. A story drafted that already has steps keeps them, as a rewrite keeps them; the draft proposes no more beyond the one Spec follow-up, and proposes as new stories what further steps would have done.
The request is sent with the panel's "Draft" button, its primary action, or by pressing Enter in the request box, whichever label it reads; Ctrl+Enter there starts it too, and the button's tooltip gives Enter as its shortcut. Shift+Enter adds a new line in the box and sends nothing. A request that is empty, or only spaces and new lines, starts nothing, and the button is disabled while it is. While a run is going, Enter starts no second one, and the button is disabled. Enter in the request box only ever sends the request: the list's Enter, opening or closing the focused story, never fires while focus is in the box.

## Drafting With Agent

Several stories can be drafted at once, each in a run of its own. "Draft with agent" is an item of the menu of every card in Draft, the Backlog, and Next sprint, the menu its hover button opens and right-clicking opens at the pointer, as the parts say, and a button of the bulk bar, drafting every selected story; a card in Current sprint or Done, and a finding, has no such item. It is meant mainly for Draft's rough stories, but drafts any story it is offered on.
Each story drafts as "Ask agent" drafts an open story, with no request box and nothing to type: the run is told the story's title, its prompt, its mode, and its steps, and asked to turn it into a full story, a fuller prompt, the mode that fits it, its Spec follow-up step where it needs one, and its spec citations, shaped as drafting says, grounded as the spec grounding says; and, where the story holds more than one piece of work, to split it, as drafting says: the story's rewrite, the first piece, with its steps, then a "New story" proposal for each other piece, each with its own title, prompt, mode, and spec citations, grounded the same way. A story that is one piece of work gets only its rewrite and its steps. Each run is its own, in a run of its own with no session, a Question run as the proposals say, with the planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts). All the runs start at once, none waiting on another, however many stories are drafted; one ending, failing, or being stopped never touches the others. A story already drafting is skipped, so drafting it again starts no second run.
The drafts never take over the side panel, which holds only one thing at a time, as the layout says: a story drafting this way shows its run on its own card, and opening the story while it drafts shows the story in the panel as ever, its run going on. While its run goes, the card's property row shows the loading state, as the states say, "Drafting…" with its spinner, in place of its status, and its menu has "Stop", which stops that run alone and keeps whatever it had proposed by then, in place of "Draft with agent". A run that fails shows its error on that card, beneath its property row, as the states say, in the theme's error colour with "Details" collapsed and "Try again", which drafts the story again; the error stays until the story is drafted again or opened. A run cut off when the application quits, as every run is, shows the same error once it is open again.
When a run ends, its card's property row shows how many of its proposals are waiting, as "3 proposals", in the theme's accent, or "1 proposal", counting down as each is decided and gone once none is left, counting every kind: its rewrite, its additions, and its new stories; a run that proposed nothing shows "Nothing proposed", muted, until the story is next opened. Opening the story shows them all in the side panel, beneath the story's own fields, under a "Proposals" heading, as proposal cards, as the proposal cards say, each new story's card labelled "New story", in the order the run gave them, its rewrite first, then its new stories and additions in the order given, with "Accept all" and "Reject all" beneath the last; "Accept all" accepts the rewrite, every addition, and every new story together. Drafting a story again while proposals of its wait adds the new ones after them.
A story's waiting proposals are kept until each is decided, saved with the plan as soon as its run ends, in `.suspense/planning/proposals/`, a file per story named by its id, so they come back, and its card's count with them, after closing Planning, a reload, or a restart. A story deleted takes its waiting proposals with it, and one duplicated copies none.
Nothing reaches the plan until it is accepted, as the proposals say. Accepting the story's rewrite rewrites it as proposed, and accepting an addition adds its step to the story's end, as the proposal cards say. Accepting a new story split off it adds that story at the end of the Backlog, marked "From agent", as the proposal cards say, never into Draft and never into Next sprint. A story in Draft whose rewrite or addition is accepted moves to the end of the Backlog, as "Move to backlog" moves it and motion animates it, staying open if it was; accepting a new story split off it never moves it, and a story in the Backlog or Next sprint stays where it is. A story sent while its proposals waited can no longer be rewritten or added to, as the proposal cards say.

## Proposals

The agent never writes the plan itself. // The prompt for Planning's drafting, asking the harness to propose
// stories grounded in the project's spec, never to write the plan: the
// request, how to search the spec, the stories in the plan, the story asked
// about where there is one, the reply asked for, then what is wanted under
// its heading. Drafting one story with the agent asks for what `story` says
// in place of a request typed, and a draft about a story is told how to
// split it, as `split` says. <reference> is filled in with where the compiled reference
// is, and <spec> with the spec location, which citations point into.

export anchor Planning:
    request:
        Below is what someone wants done in their project, in their own words.
        Propose the concrete tasks it needs: pieces of work each sent to a
        coding agent on its own, in the order they should be done, few and
        whole, one for each thing they would check off. Read the project as
        you need to, but change nothing: you only propose, and the person
        decides what goes into their plan. Each proposal says where it goes:
        a new story of its own, or added to one of the stories listed below,
        as a further step of it. Give each a short title, a prompt saying
        what should be true once it is done, in their own terms, and the mode
        it is sent in: chain to change the spec and then the code to match
        it, code to change only the code, spec to change only the spec, ask
        for a question that changes nothing, or freeform to pass the prompt
        to the agent as it is written. Prefer chain for new behaviour.

    grounding:
        A story is never written from the request alone. Before proposing,
        search the project's spec for what each story touches: the
        requirements and behaviours it changes or relies on, the names it
        uses, as a feature, a component, or a property, and the sections they
        are in. Read the spec from its compiled reference, the Markdown under
        <reference>, or from what piton slice prints for one thing, never
        from the Piton source. Cite only what you found: each citation is a
        link to the element in the spec's Piton source, under <spec>: the .pi
        file, relative to the project directory, then # and the anchor or the
        property on one it names, in the form piton slice takes, as
        <spec>/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint. Work out each
        element's file from what piton slice prints for it, which names the
        file each declaration is in, and never read the Piton source to learn
        what it says. Begin each citation with what kind of element it is,
        Requirement, Behaviour, Name, or Section, then the link, then a short
        line of what in it the story touches, then, in double quotes, the few
        words of the spec it rests on. The story's prompt names those
        elements and links to them in the same form, so the run it is sent
        to reads them first. Where nothing in the spec matches part of a
        story, never make one up: give an entry reading No match, with what
        you looked for, and say plainly in the prompt that the spec has
        nothing on it yet, so the change is new.

    stories: The stories in the plan, by id, that can be added to

    about: The story this is about, which proposals should add to where they belong to it

    story:
        Turn the story above into a full story, ready to be sent. It may be
        only a rough note: a title, or a line or two. Propose its rewrite,
        with target rewrite: a short title, a fuller prompt saying what
        should be true once it is done, the mode that fits it, and its spec
        citations. Then propose each further step it needs, in order, each
        a block of its own whose target is the story's id, a piece of the
        story done after the one before. Propose no step it already has.

    split:
        First judge whether the story above is one piece of work or several:
        separate pieces of work, each one someone would send and check off
        on its own. Where it holds several, split it: propose the story's
        rewrite, with target rewrite, as the first piece, then that piece's
        steps, each with the story's id as its target, then a block with
        target new for each other piece, a story of its own with its own
        short title, mode, spec citations, found and cited as above, and
        prompt. Never split one piece of work into several stories only to
        make them smaller: steps are for the pieces of one story, and new
        stories are for separate work. A story that is one piece of work
        gets only its rewrite and its steps, and no new story.

    splitExample: A story split in two, its rewrite with a step of its own and a new story for the other piece, is proposed as:

    reply:
        Give each proposal as a fenced code block whose info string is
        suspense-story, holding a line each for its title, its mode, and its
        target, new for a new story, the id of the story to add to, or
        rewrite to rewrite the story this is about in place, then a
        spec line followed by its citations, one per line, each begun with a
        dash, then a blank line and its prompt, as this one is:

    wanted: What is wanted

3:Everything in Planning is laid out on one rhythm, so the board scans at a glance. The board fills the body beneath the tab bar, with 24 pixels of padding at its top, sides, and foot. Its columns are all the same fixed width, 320 pixels, 16 pixels apart, each as tall as the board, set side by side from its left edge in the order work moves, Draft, the first, Backlog, Next sprint, Current sprint, Done, and Findings, the last. Each column is a list, as Trello draws one: a container of its own, as the parts draw a list, on the theme's recessed surface, one step from the base the board is on, its corners rounded 8 pixels, with its heading and its cards inside it, and no border. Three things set a list apart from the board's base, all quieter than any card's state: its recessed surface; the theme's pressed bevel around it, inside its rounded corners, so it reads as sunk into the base; and the 16 pixel gaps between columns. Each column also has a look of its own, telling it from its neighbours: a 2 pixel edge along the list's top, inside its rounded corners and above its heading, in the colour its status icon uses, as the parts give it, laid over the recessed surface at 50%, so Draft's is tertiary text, as the Backlog's is, the two told apart by their icons, Next sprint's secondary text, Current sprint's the accent, Done's success, and Findings' secondary text. The edge is the only place a column's colour shows besides its icon: its heading, its name, its cards, its empty state, and the drag placeholder keep their own surfaces and colours untouched, the placeholder its well surface. Laid over at half strength and 2 pixels tall, a column's edge is always quieter than a card's hover, its selected surface, its focus ring, or the open story's 3 pixel accent line, as the Theme's hierarchy orders decoration below state.
9:While paused, the pause bar runs across the top of the whole board, above every column, as the paused section says, beside the side panel when it is open, never over it. Each column is headed as above, so nothing sits outside the rhythm, and an open story, a drafting or research panel, and the citations and steps inside a story all use the same five parts, below.
14:- A list: one per column, as the layout places it, 320 pixels wide and as tall as the board, on the theme's recessed surface, one step from the base, with no border, the theme's pressed bevel inside its edges, its corners rounded 8 pixels, 8 pixels of padding; a 2 pixel edge along its top, in its status icon's colour laid over the recessed surface at 50%, as the layout says, the column's one look of its own; its heading row at its top, as the layout says, then its cards, or its empty state centred beneath its heading; its heading's status icon one per column, each always the same: Draft a pencil in the theme's tertiary text colour, a drawn glyph and never a circle, so it can't be mistaken for the Backlog's; the Backlog a dashed circle in the theme's tertiary text colour; Next sprint an empty circle in the theme's secondary text colour; Current sprint a half-filled circle in the theme's accent; Done a filled circle with a check in the theme's success colour; and Findings a magnifying glass in the theme's secondary text colour; each, with the list's top edge in its colour, telling its column apart at a glance while still only repeating the column's name, never standing for it alone
15:- A story card: a box the full inner width of its list, on the theme's raised surface, with a 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour, corners rounded 6 pixels, 8 pixels of padding above and below and 10 at its sides, 8 pixels from the next; a top line with its drag grip, 16 pixels, in the theme's tertiary text colour, at its left, its title beside it, the card's primary text, in up to two lines, cut off with an ellipsis after the second, and its menu button at its right on hover and always while it is focused; beneath the title, 4 pixels below it, a single property row, 20 pixels tall, in small muted text, of small items 8 pixels apart: its mode pill, in its mode's colour, as the PromptModes colours it, its step count, its attachment icon, each when it has them, and its status and time, right-aligned, once it has been sent; and, in Current sprint, its steps' lines beneath, as its steps say; used for every story, in every column, muted in Done. Its states are three distinct steps, as the Theme's hierarchy orders them: hovering raises it one surface step, to the theme's hover surface; the open story keeps a 3 pixel line in the theme's accent along its left edge, as the stories say, whether or not it is hovered; a selected card, as the selection below says, takes the theme's selected surface in place of its raised one, hovered or not; and focus shows the theme's focus ring, in the accent, 2 pixels around it, over any of them, so a hover is always quieter than a selection, and a selection than focus, as the Theme orders them, and the open story's line, an edge rather than a surface, reads apart from both, a card being open, selected, and focused at once without any of the three hiding another
16:- A row: 36 pixels tall, for steps in an open story and for findings; its secondary text muted and cut off with an ellipsis, its buttons small ghost buttons with labels, shown at its right on hover and always while it is focused
21:While any card is selected, the bulk bar runs across the board's foot, beneath its columns, beside the side panel when it is open, never over it nor over the board: a row 40 pixels tall, on the theme's raised surface with a 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour along its top, the columns shortening to make room as it slides up in motion's quick motion, and lengthening again as it slides away once nothing is selected. At its left it names how many are selected, as "3 selected"; at its right, labelled buttons, never icons alone, in this order: "Move to next sprint", which moves the selected stories in the Backlog to the end of Next sprint; "Move to backlog", which moves those in Draft and in Next sprint to the end of the Backlog; "Move to draft", which moves those in the Backlog to the end of Draft; "Draft with agent", which drafts each selected story in a run of its own, all at once, as drafting with the agent says; "Change mode", which opens a mode picker above it, the one a card's pill opens, setting the mode of every selected story to the one picked, their steps keeping their own; "Duplicate", which duplicates each, every copy just beneath its original, as a card's menu does; "Delete", which deletes them all after one confirmation naming how many, as "Delete 3 stories?"; and "Clear", which empties the selection. Every move keeps the stories' order, as the selection orders them, Draft's first, top to bottom, then the Backlog's, then Next sprint's, and animates as motion says; a move button is disabled, its tooltip saying why, while none of the selection is in the list it moves from. Moved stories stay selected, duplicates are not selected, and the originals stay so. The bar has no Send and sends nothing: a story still reaches work only through the sprint, as the sprint says.

Drafting now favours several stories over one story with many steps, and every step list shows the whole list with the prompt as step 1. It compiles, but 5 of the 36 planning tests fail, and I couldn't confirm that those failures predate my changes.

**Drafting.** I rewrote the request, story and split pieces of `system-prompts/planning.pi`. A draft now asks for:
- several stories, each one piece of work done by a single chain, and as a rule a Chain story;
- at most one Spec follow-up step per story;
- anything bigger as separate "New story" proposals;
- Code, Spec, Ask or Freeform only for a story that is only that kind of work;
- no extra steps for a story that already has some, beyond that one Spec follow-up.

The worked example in `split_example` (`src/planning.rs`) now shows a Chain rewrite, a Spec follow-up step and a new story.

**Steps.**
- **Open story:** the prompt editor is now row 1 of one "Steps" list, with its number and mode pill, and the further steps follow from 2. There is no separate "Prompt" label any more.
- **Current sprint, Done and finding cards:** the list starts with step 1, the story's own prompt, showing the story's own status.
- **Card step count and tooltip:** the count already included the prompt. The tooltip now lists the whole list, step 1 first.

**Build and tests.** The sandbox blocks reading `.suspense/system-prompts`, so the real tree won't build here. I built a copy under `target/` with placeholder files for those prompts. The 5 failing tests are:
- `a_dragged_card_finds_its_gap_in_the_column_under_it`
- `citations_are_read_and_checked`
- `enter_in_the_request_box_starts_the_draft`
- `states_and_keys_of_the_plan`
- `stories_are_added_where_they_will_sit`

The failures point at drag gaps, spec-element lookup, proposal parsing, and the composer's element id in `render_composer`, none of which I touched. But `src/planning.rs` isn't in this checkout's git history, so I had no original to compare against.

Other files (`src/prompt_mode.rs`, `src/theme.rs` and more) have uncommitted changes I didn't make, and I left them alone. I also touched `build.rs` to force its build script to rebuild; its contents are unchanged.
